---
title: "ADRD Drug Repurposing Study"
---

## Overview

This ongoing study leverages large-scale **CMS Medicare claims data** to identify candidate drugs for repurposing in Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias (ADRD). As **lead analyst**, I am responsible for the full analytical pipeline — from data extraction and harmonization through causal inference modeling and results interpretation.

Drug repurposing using real-world claims data offers a powerful, cost-effective approach to identifying existing medications that may slow cognitive decline or reduce ADRD-related outcomes in older adults.

---

## Research Questions

- Which existing medications are associated with reduced ADRD incidence or progression in Medicare beneficiaries?
- Can causal inference methods applied to observational claims data provide credible evidence for drug repurposing candidates?
- What is the role of comorbidities and polypharmacy in moderating these associations?

---

## Data

**CMS Medicare Claims Data**
- Large-scale administrative claims covering Medicare beneficiaries
- Includes inpatient, outpatient, carrier, and prescription drug (Part D) claims
- Data harmonization, linkage, and cleaning performed as part of analytical pipeline

---

## Statistical Methods

| Method | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Causal inference | Estimating drug effects using observational claims data |
| Propensity score methods | Controlling for confounding by indication |
| Survival analysis | Time to ADRD diagnosis or progression |
| Comorbidity adjustment | Bynum algorithm for comorbidity classification |
| Regression modeling | Association between drug exposure and outcomes |

---

## My Role

- **Lead analyst** — full responsibility for analytical pipeline and results
- Data extraction, harmonization, and cleaning from CMS Medicare claims
- Statistical analysis plan design and execution
- Comorbidity classification using the **Bynum algorithm**
- Results interpretation and manuscript contribution
